html:
The Butchulla, also written Badtjala, are an Aboriginal Australian people of K'gari, the great sand island off the Queensland coast, and a small part of the mainland around Hervey Bay.

The island gave fish, shellfish, dugong and freshwater from its lakes. Their mainland neighbours were the Gubbi Gubbi and Gooreng Gooreng.

In 1836 the ship Stirling Castle was wrecked to the north, and Eliza Fraser lived among the people of the island for some weeks. Her later tales of captivity gave the island its English name, Fraser Island. Timber cutting and a mission followed in the 1800s. The island became a World Heritage site in 1992 and took back its Butchulla name, K'gari, in 2023.
sum: The Butchulla, also written Badtjala, are an Aboriginal Australian people of K'gari, the great sand island off the Queensland coast, and a small part of the mainland around Hervey Bay.
